pos.personaBrief: Bayern were a star-heavy side that controlled domestic play but in the 1975 final deliberately sat deep with Mueller as defensive midfielder and counter-attacked (Leedsista); possession was not an ideology.

pro.personaBrief: Beckenbauer's libero dashes forward carried the ball, mixing patient build-up with quick counters (Champions Journal; Cramer planning counter-attacks in 1975).

est.personaBrief: Interchanging positions and a free-roaming attacking libero (Get German Football News, Beckenbauer 'free to roam') point to fluid roles rather than fixed zones.

lar.personaBrief: The team's creativity ran through central stars (Beckenbauer, Mueller, Roth); no evidence of a winger-based game.

blo.personaBrief: No evidence of gegenpressing; the 1975 final saw Bayern refuse to play and conserve energy, with a libero behind man-markers.

mar.personaBrief: Strict man-marking era and UEFA summary say Lattek and Cramer used individual marking with Beckenbauer as libero.

pla.personaBrief: Cramer adapted the plan to Leeds in 1975 (defensive, counter-attacking), while the core identity around Beckenbauer persisted; he took over a built squad.

res.personaBrief: Bayern prioritised the European Cup, winning ugly finals (1975) and conserving energy; result over show.

sis.personaBrief: Stars like Beckenbauer and Mueller had license to roam within a team that relied on individual quality and telepathic partnerships.

jog.personaBrief: Technically gifted internationals (Beckenbauer, Mueller, Maier) but also tough defenders like Schwarzenbeck; the squad was veteran and tired by 1976.

bas.personaBrief: A veteran core of World Cup and Euro winners, many homegrown, that won European Cups through experience; the squad was past its peak by 1975/76.

lid.personaBrief: Lattek united the team and Cramer had a passive style backed by captain Beckenbauer; friendships in the squad were vital, and stars had influence.
